note: P0 (live). src/legacy.js buyTrait() fail-closes under the LIVE marks arm ('That upgrade is unavailable right now') because NO server verb existed to debit the server-owned Bounty-Marks balance — so Auto-Eat, the purchase the death sheet teaches on a player's first death, and every other TRAIT, cannot be bought at all in production. Adds public.hr_traits (trait_id pk, currency marks|gold, cost, req_trait, auto_enable) seeded BYTE-EQUAL from src/legacy.js TRAITS (auto_eat 15 marks; auto_eat_2 100 marks req auto_eat) and bound to it in BOTH directions by tests/trait-buy.mjs, plus hr_trait_buy__ungated / the rate-gated hr_trait_buy wrapper (authenticated-only; the inner and hr_engine are shut out — the accrual engine must never buy a paid trait for anybody). The caller sends a TRAIT ID and a SLOT and nothing else: price, currency and prerequisite are read from the server catalogue, the balance from the character's own row under the SAME per-character advisory lock hr_apply takes. Refusals by name: unknown_trait / already_owned (a refusal, never a charged no-op) / requires:<id> / insufficient_marks / insufficient_gold / trait_daily_cap / bad_slot / no_character / rate_limited. p_idem caches the SUCCESS envelope in player_intents (read INSIDE the lock so two simultaneous retries cannot both miss it); refusals are deliberately NOT cached, so 'you are 5 Marks short' becomes buyable the moment the Marks arrive. Journals ONE player_ledger row kind='trait' with gold_in/xp_in/qty_in/gems_in explicitly 0 (it mints nothing) — the kind list is widened by an ANCHORED INSERTION into the live constraint rather than a restatement, so it cannot delete a kind another file added. It does NOT write player_state.auto_eat_enabled/auto_eat_pct: it writes the kind='flag' trait:<id> row and then CALLS hr_set_auto_eat, keeping that function the single writer (the whole write-clamp argument of 2026-08-29-auto-eat-tiers.sql, whose GATE(e) scans every body in public, rests on it); the enable is non-fatal, so a collect_first refusal never fails a purchase. Patches hr_rpc_gate (bucket hr_trait_buy, 12/min — an unknown bucket fails CLOSED, so without it every purchase would 429) and hr_state_of (one additive top-level `traits` id array, read UNFILTERED rather than through the LIMIT-1000 progress projection, so an entitlement can never be truncated into 'you own nothing') PROGRAMMATICALLY at guarded exactly-once anchors — it carries no literal create-or-replace header for either and is therefore a member of NO derivation chain and takes over no last-toucher role. MUST run AFTER 2026-08-29-auto-eat-tiers.sql (its precondition asserts hr_auto_eat_tier + the TIERED hr_set_auto_eat body), after 2026-08-16-unlocks.generated.sql (the storable flag rows the player_progress_unlock_guard trigger polices the grant against), after 2026-08-23-bounty.sql (player_state.marks) and after 2026-08-22-companion-record.sql (the last programmatic patcher of the hr_state_of total_level anchor). NO edge redeploy — hr_trait_buy is a standalone client RPC and nothing in src/core or src/data changed. Reversibility: additive — drop the two functions and hr_traits, and re-apply 2026-08-22-companion-record.sql to restore hr_state_of without the traits key; already-written rows are ordinary kind='flag' rows hr_auto_eat_tier reads regardless. §8 PROVES on apply, in an HR819-rolled-back subtransaction: unknown trait refused; tier II without tier I refused by name and charging nothing; tier I debits exactly 15, writes the flag, reports hr_auto_eat_tier=1, switches auto-eat on at the clamped 25% ceiling; replay on the same idem returns the original envelope with no second debit; a different key for an owned trait answers already_owned; a short purchase is refused AND not cached; tier II then reports tier 2 and both ids in `owned`; exactly two ledger rows; the envelope projects both; and a second FRESH character owns nothing and is sold nothing (the control).
